description: An operator's number of scans is the total of the `scancount` field over their records.

c.request: Look at the operators (`scans.crewref`) whose average file size per minute, computed per scan as `gbsize` ÷ `spanmin` with missing values ignored, is above the simple average of that figure across all operators. In a single row, how many scans have these operators done on average, what is their average GB per minute, and by how much on average do they exceed the all-operator figure? Don't round. An operator's number of scans is the total of the `scancount` field over their records.
c.sql: WITH operator_stats AS (SELECT crewref, SUM(scancount) AS scan_total, AVG(gbsize / NULLIF(spanmin, 0)) AS gb_per_minute FROM scans GROUP BY crewref), overall AS (SELECT AVG(gb_per_minute) AS all_operator_gb_per_minute FROM operator_stats) SELECT AVG(o.scan_total) AS avg_scans, AVG(o.gb_per_minute) AS avg_gb_per_minute, AVG(o.gb_per_minute - a.all_operator_gb_per_minute) AS avg_excess_gb_per_minute FROM operator_stats o CROSS JOIN overall a WHERE o.gb_per_minute > a.all_operator_gb_per_minute;

a.request: For each operator (`scans.crewref`), find their total number of scans by adding up `scancount` across their scan records, and find their average file size per minute, computed per scan as `gbsize` ÷ `spanmin`. Ignore missing values. Consider only operators whose average GB per minute is above the simple average of that figure across all operators. In a single row, give the average total number of scans of those operators, their average GB per minute, and their average margin above the all-operator average, with no rounding.
a.sql: WITH operator_stats AS (SELECT crewref, SUM(scancount) AS total_scans, AVG(gbsize / NULLIF(spanmin, 0)) AS avg_gb_per_minute FROM scans GROUP BY crewref), overall AS (SELECT AVG(avg_gb_per_minute) AS all_operator_avg FROM operator_stats) SELECT AVG(o.total_scans) AS avg_total_scans, AVG(o.avg_gb_per_minute) AS avg_gb_per_minute, AVG(o.avg_gb_per_minute - a.all_operator_avg) AS avg_margin_above_overall FROM operator_stats AS o CROSS JOIN overall AS a WHERE o.avg_gb_per_minute > a.all_operator_avg;

b.request: Group scans by `crewref`; for each operator, sum `scancount` and average `gbsize / spanmin` over scans with nonmissing values. Keep operators whose rate exceeds the unweighted average of operator rates, then return one row with their average summed `scancount`, average rate, and average amount above the all-operator rate, without rounding
b.sql: WITH operator_stats AS (SELECT crewref, SUM(scancount) AS total_scancount, AVG(gbsize / NULLIF(spanmin, 0)) AS rate FROM scans GROUP BY crewref), overall AS (SELECT AVG(rate) AS average_rate FROM operator_stats) SELECT AVG(o.total_scancount) AS average_scancount, AVG(o.rate) AS average_rate, AVG(o.rate - a.average_rate) AS average_above_all_operators FROM operator_stats o CROSS JOIN overall a WHERE o.rate > a.average_rate;

d.request: For each operator (`scans.crewref`), calculate average GB per minute from each scan’s `gbsize ÷ spanmin`, ignoring missing values, and calculate their number of scans as the sum of `scancount` over their records. For operators whose average GB per minute exceeds the simple average across all operators, return one unrounded row showing their average number of scans, their average GB per minute, and their average excess over the all-operator figure.
d.sql: WITH operator_stats AS (SELECT crewref, SUM(scancount) AS number_of_scans, AVG(gbsize / NULLIF(spanmin, 0)) AS avg_gb_per_minute FROM scans GROUP BY crewref), overall AS (SELECT AVG(avg_gb_per_minute) AS all_operator_avg FROM operator_stats) SELECT AVG(number_of_scans) AS avg_number_of_scans, AVG(avg_gb_per_minute) AS avg_gb_per_minute, AVG(avg_gb_per_minute - all_operator_avg) AS avg_excess_gb_per_minute FROM operator_stats CROSS JOIN overall WHERE avg_gb_per_minute > all_operator_avg;
